insight.title: The Singer Who Used M&Ms to Prevent a Stage Collapse
insight.subtitle: How a rock band’s ridiculous backstage demand actually saved lives.
insight.notificationHook: Why a rock band banned brown M&Ms

sections.text: In the 1980s, Van Halen’s concert contract famously demanded a bowl of M&Ms backstage, with every single brown candy painstakingly removed. Venues called them spoiled, demanding divas.
But singer David Lee Roth wasn’t being petty. The band’s massive, heavy stage equipment required precise electrical and structural setup, which local crews often ignored.
If Roth found a single brown M&M, he knew the venue staff hadn’t read the technical manual, signaling potential life-threatening safety errors on the stage.
A trivial mistake often reveals a fatal flaw.
